source_identity.canonical_title: La négation des discriminations systémiques est au mieux le reflet d'une incompréhension, au pire une stratégie politique

translation.canonical_title: Denial of systemic discrimination reflects misunderstanding in the better case and is a political strategy in the worse case
translation.displayed_title: Denial of systemic discrimination reflects misunderstanding in the better case and is a political strategy in the worse case
translation.summary:
The concept of systemic discrimination is subject to many misunderstandings and much misinformation, whether intentional or not. Contrary to what is often said, it is simply not a claim that 100% of men are bad and 100% of women are good people; rather, it is an observation according to which society is structured to offer privileges to people belonging to the male social group: more opportunities, less exposure to violence, fewer unjust exclusions, and so on. This is attributable to the fact that, for millennia, men held a monopoly on power and therefore had every interest in maintaining the privileges that had enabled them to gain access to it, as well as in demonizing groups seeking to abolish those privileges. This implies several things:

* Men are not responsible for their birth privileges.
* Men can be in a position to fight their privileges, but will pay a heavy price if they do.
* Some women derive an admittedly relative benefit from being active accomplices in their own oppression (see Right-Wing Women by Andrea Dworkin).
